about.title: Capitola Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a faulty appliance, a poorly designed tool, a car part that gives out near 41st Avenue or Bay Avenue, or a piece of gear that malfunctions without warning. In Capitola, a small beach town in Santa Cruz County, residents and visitors alike use countless consumer products daily, and when one of them is defective, the injuries can be serious. California law generally allows injured people to pursue strict liability claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers without having to prove negligence — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That's a meaningful difference from many other injury claims. If you were hurt by something that malfunctioned, broke, or lacked adequate warnings, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases and can review what happened.
commonInjuries: Burns from malfunctioning appliances or electronics
Lacerations from broken or shattered components
Crush or amputation injuries from faulty machinery
Traumatic brain injury from defective safety equipment
Chemical exposure or poisoning from mislabeled products
Fractures from collapsing furniture or unstable gear

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Law

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and caused your injury. This can make it easier to move forward without getting buried in proving intent or negligence.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers can potentially be held liable for a defective product. An independent attorney can help sort out who was involved in getting that product to you.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Keeping the item, its packaging, and any related paperwork can matter a great deal to a product liability case. An attorney can advise you on how to handle and store evidence properly from the start.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often proceed under strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, not that the company was careless. An independent attorney can look at your situation and explain which legal theories might apply.

items.question: I was hurt by a product I bought online while in Capitola — does that change anything?
items.answer: Not fundamentally. Whether a defective product was bought locally, ordered online, or borrowed from someone else, the same basic strict liability principles under California law generally apply. What matters most is preserving the product and documenting how the injury happened.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try not to throw it away, alter it, or attempt repairs. Keeping the product in its post-injury condition, along with packaging, receipts, or manuals, can be important for any later evaluation. An independent attorney can advise you on safe storage and next steps.
